text:
maria_support: FYI, escalation from AcmePayments — in some streaming responses the toolcall args arrive as partial JSON and the downstream service rejects them (schema validation). customer sees 400s and their payment webhook never fires.
ashwin_eng: ugh. any example payloads or a trace id?
maria_support: they pasted the client side logs, here's the snippet they captured from the SSE stream: 
```
event: message
data: {"id":"invok_123","name":"charge_card","args":{"amount":100,"currency":"USD","payment_method_id":"pm_abc"}
data: {"id":"invok_124","name":"charge_card","args":{"amount":50,"currency":"USD","payment_method_id":"pm_def"}
// next chunk arrives later: 
data: {"id":"invok_124","name":"charge_card","args":{"amount":50,"currency":"USD","payment_method_id":"pm_def"}}
```
They say sometimes the closing braces are missing until the next SSE chunk, and their validator complains. they reproduced it across our hosted api and their on-prem gateway.
ashwin_eng: does the client reassemble correctly usually? if client uses streaming parser it should concat data: lines. What transport are they using (SSE vs websocket)?
jordan_sre: they mentioned SSE. My initial thought: proxy / edge is splitting chunks mid-JSON (chunked transfer or gzip buffer). Could be nginx buffering off or intermediate CDN. Ask for capture of raw TCP or edge logs.
maria_support: asking customer for request id + gateway region + a recent timestamp. they provided request id: req_20260305_58f3 and region: us-east-1.
samir_prodeng: pinging runtime team — ashwin any guess on where our SSE emitter might cut a buffer? we flush tokens frequently but never intentionally split a single event payload.
ashwin_eng: possible places: (1) our SSE writer flush call inside the model loop, (2) platform reverse-proxy (envoy/nginx) chunking, (3) client-side SSE lib that processes line-by-line. Can we get a server-side capture for req_20260305_58f3?
jordan_sre: I pulled proxy logs for that req id: see snippets — large streaming body with Transfer-Encoding: chunked, chunk sizes look weird: "6\r\n{...\r\n4\r\n}..." Might be chunk boundaries in the middle of encoded JSON.
maria_support: customer also reported intermittent latency spikes around same time (~600ms). they suspect retries may leave partial payloads.
ashwin_eng: can customer try disabling intermediate proxies, or run a direct curl to our hosted endpoint to compare behavior? ask them to run: 
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/stream -d '{"input":"charge","stream":true}'
```
and save raw output to file, then grep for unclosed braces.
maria_support: sent instructions. customer replied with raw dump attached — they highlighted a sequence where a single data: event is split across two TCP segments and their SSE client emitted two separate events, feeding a JSON parser that errors on the first fragment.
samir_prodeng: thanks. next steps: (A) runtime team to add a small boundary-safe emission step so each event is always newline-terminated and self-contained even if chunked; (B) platform to check proxy chunking behavior and disable midstream gzip or buffering for SSE endpoints; (C) support to collect a minimal repro and indicate workaround (client-side reassembly of consecutive data: lines).
ashwin_eng: quick patch candidate: ensure we emit a trailing "\n\n" after each data block and avoid splitting inside data payload by using chunked writes aligned to event boundaries. I'll open a runtime PR.
jordan_sre: I'll file a ticket to audit envoy/nginx configs for SSE endpoints and add tests that simulate small MTU/chunk sizes.
maria_support: customer OK with workaround for now and wants ETA. please post PR/issue links here and I will update them. :thumbsup:
sre-bot: Created issue INF-4122 "SSE partial-json under chunked transfer" assigned to eng-runtime. Link: https://internal.redwood/issues/INF-4122
ashwin_eng: PR opened: https://internal.redwood/pull/7689 — includes safer event flushing + unit test for SSE chunk boundaries. Asking for review from eng-runtime.
samir_prodeng: plan to deploy a canary with the patch to us-east-1 tomorrow morning. will monitor for similar request ids.
maria_support: noted, passing ETA to customer. closing initial escalation but keeping thread open for post-canary results. :white_check_mark:
